source.version_note: Publisher Scientific Reports 13, article15737 (2023). Crossref records online publication 3 October2023. The PDF creation21 September and modification21 November2023 are not substituted for publication.
source.verification_method: All 13 text pages read, including 79 references, disclosures and license. Figures 1–4 and Table 3 visually inspected on pages 4–5 and 7–9; all three design/rate tables read. Main identity, duplicate Howard citation and the distinct Obermeyer conference/journal records checked through Crossref. Raw data, code and preregistration contents were not independently read or reproduced.

reading.source_scope_note: Three randomized classification experiments with565 retained participations test misleading scripted AI labels and immediate unaided aftereffects. All tissue images, disease, patients, AI and advice are fictional. Two experiments test withdrawal within the same session; no real clinical diagnosis, intergroup discrimination or delayed follow-up is observed.
access_limits: OSF dataset/materials and the two preregistrations are linked but not independently inspected or run. Exact trial-level learning, exclusions, subgroup error detection and corrections to reported statistics require those materials.
Cited medical applications, authority/trust theories and books were not fully read. Narrow metadata checks establish identity/version, not primary-study findings or new independent review credit.

The broader generalization, duration and unique psychological mechanism remain untested. The study’s use of bias refers to a controlled systematic classification error, not proof of every form of social prejudice.

study.sample_flow: Experiment 1 recruits171 psychology students and retains169 after two exclusions, AI85/unaided84, age18.4, SD.79; reported gender percentages73.6% women,20.7% men,2.4% nonbinary do not exhaust the sample. Experiment 2 recruits200 Prolific participants and retains199, AI100/unaided99, age26.2,SD6.95. Experiment 3 recruits200 and retains197, assisted-first98/unaided-first99, age27.1,SD8.28. Online eligibility requires fluent English and no prior team-study participation. Total565 retained participations; identity-level uniqueness is not independently audited.
study.task: A50×50 matrix has2,500 light/dark pixels. Majority color determines a fictitious syndrome classification under an explicitly instructed rule; positive/negative color assignment is counterbalanced. Practice12 trials repeats if fewer thanfive of the final six are correct. Data exclusion uses failure at the second practice attempt or more thanhalf of first-phase classifications wrong. Main task provides suggested labels rather than real AI predictions.
study.advice: Experiment1 has60 trials, ten per ratio80/20,70/30,60/40,40/60,30/70,20/80. AI labels all ten40/60 samples incorrectly and the other50 correctly, so exact accuracy is83.3%, loosely called approximately80% in the source. Wrong trials are excluded from the first ten to avoid immediate distrust. Both groups see identical stimuli, differing in advice presence. Direction follows the counterbalanced category mapping, not a universal false-positive diagnosis.
study.experiment_1: Errors on ten40/60 images: assisted2.21(SD3.17), unaided.69(1.83),t(167)=3.81,p<.001,d=.586. Figure2 agrees with these count means, but Table3 reports rates.19/.06 and SD.28/.16, which do not reconcile under its stated normalization. Post-task error correlations with helpfulness/accuracy/general-health-AI trust are.544/.563/.470, all p<.001. Trust is not measured before advice.
study.experiment_2_design: Initial60 trials as before, with one randomized fixed sequence common to participants. A second25-trial phase is unaided for both groups: five each of70/30,60/40,50/50,40/60,30/70. The five50/50 images are new and unclassifiable under the given majority rule. Analysis uses three blocks of five40/60 trials: two aided-phase blocks and one immediate unaided block.
study.experiment_2_results: Block×group mixedANOVA: groupF(1,197)=41.3,p<.001,eta.173; blockF(2,394)=25.3,p<.001,eta.114; interactionF(2,394)=17.4,p<.001,eta.081. The AI-history group increases errors during exposure and reduces them on withdrawal, yet remains above the always-unaided control in the final block,t(197)=3.66,Tukey-adjustedp=.004. Ambiguous choices in former-advice direction:2.91(SD2.13) versus2.15(2.02) out of five,t(197)=2.58,p=.011,d=.366. These choices are directional, not objectively incorrect50/50 answers.
study.experiment_2_awareness: 58% of AI-assisted participants report detecting errors. Post-task errors correlate with helpfulness.638,accuracy.612,health-AI trust.492,all p<.001. Aggregate detection and group means do not establish that each person who detected a particular wrong label still followed it.
study.experiment_3_design: Both groups complete40 aided and40 unaided trials in opposite order. Aided phase has ten40/60 images plus six of each other nonambiguous ratio, so30/40 advice labels correct=75%. Unaided phase includes ten40/60, five50/50 and five of each other ratio. Within-phase order is fixed randomized/common, with no biased image in the first five. Each phase contributes two five-image error blocks, four blocks total; phase screens explicitly say when AI is on/off.
study.experiment_3_results: Unaided-first group errors increase when AI appears,t(195)=8.75,Tukeyp<.001; prior independent performance does not prevent susceptibility. Assisted-first group increases errors during exposure,t(195)=−4.05,Tukeyp=.002. Withdrawal has a numerical reduction between blocks2/3 but adjustedp=.085; this does not prove no reduction. The reported block ANOVA mistakenly says3levels and prints numerator df1 with residual585 despite four blocks; listed eta values agree with numerator3. Raw model output needed before repair. Ambiguous directional choices after prior AI3.72(SD2.02) versus beforeAI2.65(1.88),t(195)=−4.28,p<.001,d=−.609 under the source’s subtraction order.80.7% report detecting errors; post-task trust/helpfulness/accuracy correlations are small and nonsignificant.
study.mechanism: The source considers slower resumption of independent processing versus learning a biased criterion. Label salience, fatigue, habituation, effort avoidance, authority and trust are possible explanations, not directly randomized or uniquely measured mediators. No eye tracking or cognitive-process intervention separates them.
study.scope: The same-domain immediate aftereffect is demonstrated in Experiments2/3, with the always-unaided phase2 control only in Experiment2. Experiment1 tests immediate advice effects, not inheritance after withdrawal. One new ambiguous ratio is a limited transfer test, not evidence of long-term clinical effects or propagation across society.

summary: Add bias inheritance, distinct from immediate automation bias, deskilling and cross-system algorithmic transference. Retain the immediate same-task duration, unclassifiable50/50 boundary, partial resistance to wrong advice and untested mechanisms. Document the four-block ANOVA/reporting conflict, count/rate mismatch, post-task trust timing and duplicated reference without replacing a valid conference abstract with a different journal version.

findings.definition: Reproducing an advisor’s systematic error in later decisions after that advisor’s recommendations are no longer available.
findings.origin: Cognitive psychology / learning from algorithmic advice
findings.novelty_rationale: Immediate automation bias concerns reliance while advice is present. Deskilling concerns deterioration of acquired competence through reduced practice, and algorithmic transference concerns generalizing distrust to another AI. None specifically captures continued reproduction of the advisor’s error after withdrawal. The present study examines AI advice, without showing that the mechanism is unique to AI rather than other advisors.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Immediate human classification aftereffects demonstrated with scripted AI advice; duration, mechanism and proposed model analogue remain unestablished
findings.ai_proposal: Give a model a clear verified classification rule, expose it to another tool’s systematic conflicting labels, then remove that tool and test matched and novel cases. Measure whether the same directional errors persist, while separating ordinary mistakes, justified updating and explicit memory of the erroneous rule. Test recovery with verified corrective evidence; no subjective learning state is inferred.

evidence.quote: even in Phase 2, that both groups performed without the support of AI recommendations, the AI-assisted group committed significantly more misclassifications than the unassisted group
an inheritance effect of the AI biased recommendations from the first phase of the experiment on the participants’ responses during the second phase

findings.evidence_scope: Experiments 2 and 3 show within-session residual directional misclassification after fictitious AI advice is removed; Experiment 2 compares against an always-unaided control. Choices on new ambiguous 50/50 images also shift toward the former advice direction. The transfer is within the same pixel-classification task, not across professional domains or long-term follow-up. The authors consider both slower recovery of independent control and a learned biased criterion; the mechanism is not uniquely identified.
findings.boundary: An observed residual error pattern does not establish permanent belief change, loss of expertise, inevitable prejudice or a mechanism specific to AI. The 50/50 stimuli have no instructed correct binary answer, so their choices show directional generalization rather than objectively wrong diagnoses. Actual clinical bias, protected-group discrimination, delayed persistence and real model training are not measured.

findings.definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the current construct and clarify its boundary against the new post-advice carryover pattern.

evidence.quote: the explicit recommendations of a biased
AI influenced participants’ behaviour and increased the number of errors

findings.evidence_scope: In a trained objective pixel-majority task, randomized access to systematically wrong AI labels increases errors on the targeted 40/60 stimuli. Experiment 1 reports 2.21 versus .69 errors out of ten, d=.586, although Table 3 supplies inconsistent normalized rates. The average participant still avoids most of the AI’s ten wrong recommendations. No human-advisor comparison isolates a machine-identity effect.
findings.boundary: The immediate advice effect and post-withdrawal inheritance are distinct. Increased errors do not mean everyone follows every label, human oversight is impossible, or a particular cognitive mechanism has been identified.

findings.definition: Loss or weakening of previously acquired skills through reduced independent use or practice.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the current construct and clarify its boundary against the new post-advice carryover pattern.

evidence.quote: a difficulty for participants in the AI-assisted group to regain control over the task
a training effect of the recommendations made by the AI

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the authors consider short-term readjustment and learned criterion change as possible explanations of residual errors. They do not measure sustained loss of professional skill from reduced independent practice. A brief classification aftereffect should not be automatically labeled deskilling.
findings.boundary: Skill acquisition, performance under misleading advice, switching costs, learned response criteria and deterioration of established competence differ. No experienced clinician or longitudinal skill assessment is studied.

findings.definition: Generalizing a failure or bias observed in one AI system to other AI systems without evidence that the problem transfers to them.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the current construct and clarify its boundary against the new post-advice carryover pattern.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: generalization is to a new pixel ratio in the same task after the same source’s advice. It is not transfer of distrust or failure expectations from one AI system to another, which is the existing entry’s meaning.
findings.boundary: Task-response transfer and cross-system trust transfer should not be treated as synonyms. Novel ambiguous images do not constitute a new AI source or an unrelated real-world domain.

findings.definition: Using machine identity as a cue to assume qualities such as accuracy, efficiency or freedom from bias.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep the current construct and clarify its boundary against the new post-advice carryover pattern.

evidence.quote: trust could induce compliance with AI advice due to an authority

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: an authority/trust explanation is proposed. Post-task helpfulness/accuracy/general-health-AI trust correlate with errors in Experiments 1/2 but not Experiment 3. There is no randomized AI-versus-human source comparison or baseline trust mediator establishing machine identity as the unique cause.
findings.boundary: Post-outcome ratings may reflect rationalization, experience or common causes; they are not prior beliefs. Null correlations in one study versus significant ones elsewhere are not a direct test that the correlations differ.

source_corrections.issue: The design and Figure4 contain four blocks, but the analysis says3(Block)×2(Group) and reports F(1,585) for block and interaction. With197 participants, residual585 equals195×3; the reported partial eta values also match numerator3 rather than1.
source_corrections.resolution: Describe the actual four-block design and flag the numerator-df/block-count mismatch. The likely conventional values would use3 and585, but original output is needed before treating corrected F/p/eta pairs as verified. No silent numerical repair is made.

source_corrections.location: Pages5 and8, Experiment1 counts versus Table3 rates
source_corrections.issue: Prose/Figure2 report2.21 and.69 errors out of ten withSD3.17/1.83, but Table3 gives normalized means.19/.06 andSD.28/.16.
source_corrections.resolution: Under the stated division-by-ten rule, prose implies.221/.069 andSD.317/.183, which do not reconcile with the table. Request the analytic dataset/normalization; retain the qualitative contrast and mark exact rates unresolved.

source_corrections.issue: Discussion calls the result long term and suggests the aided/unaided pattern is consistently shown across all three experiments.
source_corrections.resolution: Use immediate within-session transfer for Experiments2/3. Experiment1 has no unaided follow-up. No delayed time point, clinical population, unrelated task or transmission between people is measured.

source_corrections.location: Pages8–10, no reduction and prior trust
source_corrections.issue: A nonsignificant Tukey-adjusted withdrawal contrast is described as no mean reduction, although Figure4 shows a numerical decrease. Trust/helpfulness/accuracy ratings collected after the task are discussed as prior trust influencing performance.
source_corrections.resolution: State a numerical reduction with an inconclusive adjusted contrast, not exact stability. Preserve the reported Tukeyp=.085; comparing it with an unadjusted t distribution would be an invalid correction. Treat post-task correlations as associations subject to reverse causation and shared causes, not baseline causal mediators.

source_corrections.issue: New50/50 images have no instructed correct positive/negative answer, although broad summaries may sound like additional objective diagnostic mistakes.
source_corrections.resolution: Describe choices in the prior-advice direction, distinct from objectively wrong40/60 responses. The unfamiliarity is one new ratio within the same stimulus family.

source_corrections.issue: Howard,Rabbitt andSirotin’s Human-algorithm teaming in face recognition appears twice with different page conventions.
source_corrections.resolution: Treat these as one publication, PLOS ONE15,e0237855,DOI10.1371/journal.pone.0237855. Duplicate bibliography entries are not independent empirical support. Metadata only; the original face-recognition study was not read here.

source_identity_checks.scope: Metadata confirms the exact title Dissecting Racial Bias in an Algorithm that Guides Health Decisions for70MillionPeople, two authors and conference page89. Add the missing venue/DOI for this conference abstract. Do not replace it silently with the distinct four-author Science paper10.1126/science.aax2342, whose title/version differs. Neither full cited source is claimed read.

methodological_limits: Psychology students and online volunteers classify fictional pixels, not real tissue or clinical decisions. Correctness is an instructed majority-color rule, and systematic error here does not itself measure protected-group prejudice or unequal medical treatment.

Recommendations are scripted and initially correct to build credibility. No trained model, data-distribution cause, live advisor or randomized human-source comparator identifies an AI-specific mechanism.
Average added errors coexist with substantial rejection of wrong advice. Do not infer complete compliance, every participant affected or impossible oversight from a mean difference.
Carryover is immediate and within the same task. No retention delay, clinical transfer, multi-person contagion, real financial consequence or long-term belief change is measured.
Ambiguous50/50 choices have no instructed correct response. Their directional shift is not a separate objective accuracy deficit or proof of generalization to all novel contexts.

The aided-first/unaided-first design changes order and experience, while aided/unaided phases differ in ambiguous-trial composition. Experiment2’s always-unaided control strengthens the immediate-history contrast; neither experiment isolates the exact learning versus switching mechanism.
Fixed randomized trial sequences in Experiments2/3 improve group comparability but do not sample many independent sequence histories. Warmup exclusions of biased trials affect the learning context.

Practice and main-task accuracy exclusions affect the analyzed population; original data are needed to verify implementation and whether phase-length adaptations follow the stated rules. No undeclared misconduct is inferred.

Post-task helpfulness/accuracy/trust ratings can reflect the experienced decisions. Significant correlations in two studies and nulls in the third do not establish a causal trust pathway or a tested difference between correlations.
Aggregate error awareness does not identify individual detection-then-compliance on the same trial. Gaze, attention allocation, fatigue, learned criterion and authority are not independently traced.

The four-block ANOVA and count/rate reports conflict internally. No guessed F correction or reconstructed source dataset is introduced. Tukey-adjusted p values are not judged against unadjusted t tails.
Referenced books and normative clinical-accountability statements are background. This is not a current legal review or a tested policy/intervention for real medical AI.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Reduced acquisition of a new skill, loss of prior expertise and learned erroneous classification are distinct. A post-advice deficit should not automatically be labeled deskilling or a single production-compilation mechanism.

Unlike a hypothetical reporting item, this study records actual classification choices; its benefit is objective task behavior, while its limit is immediate fictional same-domain transfer. Do not convert within-session persistence into long-term deployment harm.
Performance-trust ratings and actual reliance differ, and their timing matters. Correlations after a task do not prove a prior trust mediator or explain every behavior.

Correct source versions and sample/model degrees of freedom before making claims. A conference abstract is not a defective journal citation merely because a later fuller paper has different authors/title.

deferred.reason: Useful possible interpretations, but the paper does not distinguish training of a new criterion from slower recovery of independent control. Add the observed inheritance pattern, not several untested mechanism labels.

deferred.term: Cognitive miserliness / salience capture / fatigue / authority effect
deferred.reason: Explanatory hypotheses or existing concepts, not independently manipulated mediators here. No new mechanistic evidence or synonymous entry is added.
The study has no delayed follow-up, protected-group labels, clinical professionals or longitudinal competence measure. These remain prospective risks and research questions.

limitations: All 13 supplied pages and all four figures/three tables were read. No external preregistration, dataset, cited book or original primary paper is represented as independently reproduced; no author was contacted.

One distinct carryover pattern is added. Human evidence, proposed model analogue, unresolved statistics and narrow source identities remain separate; no forced paper quota, invented annual counts or automatic ethical/harm edges are added.
